{{nihongo|'''Asō Shrine'''|阿宗神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

'''Aso Shrine''' (あそうじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Hiroyama, Honda-chō, {{ill|Tatsuno, Hyōgo|Q877190|qid=Q877190}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}.

=== History ===
In the 32nd year of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|qid=Q329792}}, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} was established on {{ill|Mount Tatsuoka|Q11597851|qid=Q11597851}} after being invited from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangū}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}}, it was relocated to its present site in Hiroyama. In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, it was known as '''Hiroyama Hachimangū'''. A small shrine continued to exist at the former site on Tateokayama, but the old Aso Shrine gradually declined and was transferred to the present Aso Shrine site in the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|lt=mid-Meiji period}}, at which time the Hiroyama Hachimangū was renamed Aso Shrine. Until the early Meiji period, it was a shrine administered by {{ill|Ikaruga-dera Temple|Q11500736|qid=Q11500736|lt=Ikaruga-dera}} of the {{ill|Tiantai|Q668188|qid=Q668188}} as its {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755|lt=temple administrator}}, and there was no resident {{ill|Kannushi|Q60523|qid=Q60523}}. It was formerly designated a Shinsen Heihaku-ryō Kyōshinsha.

=== Chronology ===
* {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|qid=Q329792}} 32 ({{ill|571|Q30475|qid=Q30475}}): {{ill|Ōtomo no Satehiko|Q15043483|qid=Q15043483}} received an imperial command and invited a divided spirit of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangū}} to {{ill|Mount Tatsuoka|Q11597851|qid=Q11597851}}.
* {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|qid=Q1346307}} 8 ({{ill|764|Q31163|qid=Q31163}}): Fujiwara no Sadakuni performed prayers for the subjugation of the Silla army.
* {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}): Listed as a minor shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}.
* {{ill|Bunji (era)|Q1194415|qid=Q1194415}} 5 ({{ill|1189|Q19735|qid=Q19735}}): The lord of Uchiyama Castle, Shiotsu Yoshitsuna<ref>Grandson of Shiotsu Tarō, the eldest son of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|Q3083118|qid=Q3083118|lt=Shinra Saburō Yoshimitsu}}. In Bunji 2 ({{ill|1186|Q19730|qid=Q19730}}), he moved from {{ill|Ōmi Province|ca|Província d'Ōmi|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆمی|cs|Provincie Ómi|de|Provinz Ōmi|es|Provincia de Ōmi|fa|ولایت اومی|fi|Ōmin provinssi|fr|Province d'Ōmi|gl|Provincia de Ōmi|hak|Ōmi-koet|id|Provinsi Ōmi|it|Ōmi|ja|近江国|ko|오미국|lt|Omio žemė|nl|Omi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Ōmi|pt|Província de Ōmi|ru|Оми (провинция)|simple|Ōmi Province|sk|Ómi (provincia)|sr|Провинција Оми|tr|Ōmi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Омі|vi|Tỉnh Ōmi|zh|近江國|zh_min_nan|Ômi-kok|zh_yue|近江國|qid=Q843882}} to Uchiyama in {{ill|Ibo District, Hyōgo|Q1042150|qid=Q1042150}} by an order of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}}. Shiotsu Saemon-no-suke Yoshimoto later moved to Hiroyama during the {{ill|Entoku|Q431465|qid=Q431465}} era and became the ancestor of the Shiotsu family. “Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer.”</ref> relocated the shrine to its present site in Hiroyama Village, {{ill|Ittō district|Q11498435|qid=Q11498435}}.
* {{ill|Bun'ei|Q1010103|qid=Q1010103}} 3 ({{ill|1266|Q5517|qid=Q5517}}): Rebuilt due to storm damage to the shrine buildings; came under the administration of Rakurakusan Enshō-ji as bettō-ji, and the festival featuring a mikoshi procession began (previously, Kiuchiyama Tayū and Ayabe Takenoshin served as shrine guardians).
* {{ill|Shōō (Kamakura period)|Q1327371|qid=Q1327371}} 1 ({{ill|1288|Q5550|qid=Q5550}}): The founder of the {{ill|Ji-shu|Q696966|qid=Q696966}}, {{ill|Ippen|Q1056232|qid=Q1056232}}, dedicated a waka poem.
* {{ill|Kenmu|Q1193970|qid=Q1193970|lt=Kenmu}} 3 ({{ill|1336|Q6028|qid=Q6028}}): {{ill|Nitta Yoshisada|Q1328796|qid=Q1328796}} established his headquarters here in preparation for the subjugation of {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|Q297107|qid=Q297107}}.
* {{ill|Kakei|Q1145253|qid=Q1145253|lt=Kakitsu}} 2 ({{ill|1388|Q6365|qid=Q6365}}), March: The provincial governor, former governor of Echigo, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Akamatsu Akinori}}, donated rice fields.
* {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} 6 ({{ill|1537|Q6461|qid=Q6461}}): Rakurakusan Enshō-ji was abolished, and {{ill|Ikaruga-dera Temple|Q11500736|qid=Q11500736|lt=Ikaruga-dera}} replaced it as bettō-ji.
* Tenbun 10 ({{ill|1541|Q6516|qid=Q6516}}), December 2: Shrine buildings and subsidiary shrines were destroyed by warfare.
* {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853}} 18 ({{ill|1549|Q6554|qid=Q6554}}): The local deputy steward, Sudō Munetsugu, rebuilt the torii gate.
* {{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064}} 3 ({{ill|1572|Q6670|qid=Q6670}}), October 25: Shrine buildings were destroyed by fire.
* {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 2 ({{ill|1574|Q6680|qid=Q6680}}), September: Rebuilt as '''Hiroyama Hachimangū'''.
* {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 12 ({{ill|1607|Q6756|qid=Q6756}}): The dance hall and worship hall were rebuilt.
* {{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} 5 ({{ill|1793|Q7807|qid=Q7807}}): The roof of the main hall was replaced, and the lord of {{ill|Tatsuno Castle|Q10856352|qid=Q10856352}} of the Ikoma clan donated three tan of rice fields for offerings.
* {{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka}} 7 ({{ill|1810|Q6922|qid=Q6922}}): Records note that the 1500th memorial festival of Hachimangū was held and sumō matches were sponsored.
* Bunka 8 ({{ill|1811|Q6928|qid=Q6928}}): Suzutora Nuidono of the Kyoto {{ill|Yoshida family|Q11413722|qid=Q11413722}} ({{ill|Yoshida Shintō|Q1760351|qid=Q1760351}}) issued an official Shikinaisha certificate during an inspection tour.
* {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 3 ({{ill|1832|Q7584|qid=Q7584}}): The lord of Tatsuno Domain, Wakisaka Awaji-no-kami, performed prayers for rain.
* {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} period: Renamed '''Aso Shrine'''.
* Meiji 7 ({{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}}), February (also recorded as April of Meiji 4): Ranked as a village shrine.
* Meiji 13 ({{ill|1880|Q7806|qid=Q7806}}): Reconstruction of the heiden and haiden was completed, and a formal relocation ceremony and special festival were held.
* Meiji 14 ({{ill|1881|Q7808|qid=Q7808}}), June: Promoted to prefectural shrine.
* {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 5 ({{ill|1916|Q2087|qid=Q2087}}): Designated as a Shinsen Heihaku-ryō Kyōshinsha.

=== On-site information ===
; Address
* 492 {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hiroyama, Honda-chō}}, {{ill|Tatsuno, Hyōgo|Q877190|qid=Q877190}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}

; Access
* From JR {{ill|Kishin Line|Q869221|qid=Q869221}} {{ill|Hon-Tatsuno Station|Q11520740|qid=Q11520740}}, about a 20-minute walk (1.5 km south).
* From JR {{ill|San'yō Main Line|Q1193436|qid=Q1193436}}, {{ill|San'yō Shinkansen|Q615964|qid=Q615964}}, or {{ill|Bantan Line|Q910359|qid=Q910359}} {{ill|Himeji Station|Q119301|qid=Q119301}}, or {{ill|Sanyo Electric Railway Main Line|Q871058|qid=Q871058|lt=Sanyō Dentetsu Line}} {{ill|Sanyo-Himeji Station|Q7420806|qid=Q7420806}}, take a {{ill|Shinki Bus|Q11589421|qid=Q11589421}} bound for Tatsuno and get off at Hiroyama bus stop (immediately nearby).
* From {{ill|Japan National Route 2|Q1131340|qid=Q1131340}} via the {{ill|Prince Tatsuno bypass|Q11443881|qid=Q11443881}}, exit at Fukuda Ramp and proceed north on {{ill|Japan National Route 179|Q6156867|qid=Q6156867}}. (Parking available: 10 spaces)
